verdict_text: NO. The merge is applied sequentially rather than both task vectors against the unmodified base, violating required result clause 2. The script computes `tmp = b + λ(f1 - b)` and then `out = tmp + λ(f2 - tmp)`, so the second task vector is taken against the already-merged tensor; expanding gives `b + λ(f1-b) + λ(f2-b) - λ²(f1-b)`, i.e. the result is short by `0.16 * (ft1 - base)` on every one of the 48 MLP tensors. This is exactly the ordering hazard the specification calls out, and the error is far larger than the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance in the grading criteria. The verification, merged-count and 160-tensor checks are otherwise correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
